extracted.intended_audience: ProPublica employees, editorial staff, and editorial contributors
extracted.subtask_description: Organization-specific code of ethics and conduct for ProPublica newsroom and contributors, covering standards for reporting, conflicts of interest, use of AI, financial and political activity, confidentiality, and enforcement procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth as North Star / Accuracy and Independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Our facts are accurate and fairly presented; our analyses represent our best independent judgments rather than our preferences or those of our sources; there are no hidden agendas in any of our journalistic undertakings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The code emphasizes that telling the truth and earning readers' belief is essential. If readers cannot assume accuracy, independent judgment, and absence of hidden agendas, ProPublica cannot succeed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source identification and anonymous sources
rubrics_metrics.description: We strive to identify all the sources of our information, shielding them with anonymity only when they insist upon it and when they provide vital information — not opinion or speculation; when there is no other way to obtain that information; and when we know the source is knowledgeable and reliable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To the extent possible, identify any important bias a source may have. Editors should assess appropriateness of unnamed sources and may ask to know their identity; sources must understand this practice. When a source chooses anonymity, editors and reporters should take special care to verify authenticity. Do not say that a person declined to comment when he or she is quoted anonymously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify bias of sources
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent that we can, we identify in our stories any important bias such a source may have.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include explanation of important biases alongside sourced information so readers can assess credibility and perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document provenance disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: If the story hinges on documents, as opposed to interviews, we describe how the documents were obtained, at least to the extent possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When documents are central to reporting, provide transparency about their sourcing to bolster trust and allow independent assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: No misrepresentation in reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: We don’t misidentify or misrepresent ourselves to get a story. When we seek an interview, we identify ourselves as ProPublica journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When testing computer systems (algorithms, websites), creating user profiles that conform to subject characteristics is permitted only when necessary and only for testing purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI use principles
rubrics_metrics.description: When using artificial intelligence in our newsroom, we are careful to ensure we never violate the trust readers place in us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific principles: (1) We are responsible for everything we publish, and work done by AI must be reviewed by staff. (2) We must verify any AI-generated material. (3) We must be transparent about any meaningful role AI has played in our work. (4) We must not use AI to generate or manipulate content in a way that could mislead our audience, and AI tools don’t replace the original reporting, analysis and judgment of our journalists. (5) We must be sure that our use of AI does not compromise our sources, subjects or data.

rubrics_metrics.name: No payment for interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: We don’t pay for interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment for interviews is prohibited to avoid compromising source motivations and credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: No plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: We don’t plagiarize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All material must be original or properly attributed; plagiarism is forbidden.

rubrics_metrics.name: No fabrication; no composite characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in our work should be fabricated. We don’t use composite characters or fictional ages, places or dates in our stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default for identifying sources is by full names; pseudonyms can only be used in extraordinary situations with the approval of the editor in chief or a managing editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default to full identification of sources; pseudonyms only rarely
rubrics_metrics.description: Our default for identifying sources is by using full names; pseudonyms can only be used in extraordinary situations with the approval of the editor in chief or a managing editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pseudonyms reserved for extraordinary cases; editors must approve, ensuring justification and verification steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of donor-subject relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: If we become aware that a subject of a story is also a ProPublica donor, we disclose that relationship in the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency about donor relationships is required to avoid perceived conflicts of interest in reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness in reporting and seeking response
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall, we must be fair. Investigative reporting requires special diligence with respect to fairness. Whenever we portray someone in a negative light, we should make a real effort to obtain a response from that person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give subjects a reasonable amount of time to respond before publication; what is 'reasonable' may depend on urgency and competitiveness. If parties aren’t reached, explain in the story what efforts were made to contact them. Fairness includes completeness and honesty — do not omit major facts or mislead readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data verification and correction explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever we publish data, we should make diligent efforts to verify and validate the integrity of the data set and explain how to correct any inaccuracies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure data provenance, validation steps, and correction mechanisms are described so readers can assess reliability and correct errors where found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness — do not omit major facts
rubrics_metrics.description: No story is fair if it omits facts of major importance or significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fairness includes completeness; ensure essential facts are included to avoid misleading the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections — correct mistakes promptly and fully
rubrics_metrics.description: When mistakes are made, they need to be corrected — fully, quickly and ungrudgingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond to any question of fairness or accuracy by discussing with supervising editor and deciding appropriate response; correct promptly and transparently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of internal and unpublished information
rubrics_metrics.description: Any and all information and other material obtained by a ProPublica employee in connection with his or her employment is strictly the property of ProPublica ... Such material should never be disclosed to anyone outside ProPublica ... until such information has been made available to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidential company matters should not be discussed with family or acquaintances or in places where one can be overheard; divulge internally only to those who need to know.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid appearance of market manipulation or trading on non-public information
rubrics_metrics.description: All employees shall be expected to avoid behavior that leaves no grounds for belief, or even suspicion, that the creation, dissemination, or non-dissemination of news was influenced by a desire to affect the price of any security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employees must avoid speculation or the appearance of speculation based on non-public information, including short-selling, buying/selling futures or options, and making investments in anticipation of ProPublica coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cryptocurrency investment restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: All employees must be careful when making cryptocurrency investments. The holding of memecoins or speculative assets connected to specific public figures or news events is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits speculative crypto holdings tied to news/events or public figures to avoid conflicts and appearance of trading on editorial information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gambling and prediction markets restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: While betting on sporting events and taking part in small-stakes, friendly contests are permissible when legal and when employees are not involved in coverage, no employee should wager on the outcome of news events on the prediction markets — regardless of whether or not they are involved in coverage of said event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation in prediction markets on news outcomes is forbidden to prevent conflicts and appearance of profiting from editorial information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Securities restrictions for editorial personnel covering an industry
rubrics_metrics.description: No editorial personnel assigned to cover a specific industry may buy or sell securities in any company engaged, in whole or significant part, in that industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to buying, selling or holding mutual funds or ETFs that invest predominantly in the specific industry; broad-based funds are allowed. Editorial personnel reporting a story that could affect the price of an individual security they own must disclose the ownership to their editor or supervisor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment disclosures and reassignment/recusal
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon being hired, and from time to time during employment, editorial personnel will be asked to affirm that they have no investments or business dealings that would violate this code with respect to the assignment they are being given ... If the employee is unable to make this affirmation, the employee may choose to sell the relevant holdings or will be reassigned to avoid any potential conflict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employees must also affirm that, to the best of their knowledge, no spouse, immediate family or partner has holdings that might reasonably raise doubts; employees have an active duty to raise potential concerns with managers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gifts, entertainment and benefits policy
rubrics_metrics.description: ProPublica employees should not offer or provide ... any gift, entertainment or reimbursement of expenses of more than nominal value ... Nor should employees offer or provide ... any material, equipment or services to any individual in a position to make or influence any business, philanthropic or governmental decision affecting ProPublica.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversely, employees should not solicit or accept any payment, loan, services, equipment or any other benefit of more than nominal value from suppliers, vendors, or anyone with an actual or prospective business relationship. For instance, acceptance of free trips is prohibited; do not seek or accept preferential treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on serving as corporate directors or officers
rubrics_metrics.description: ProPublica employees may not serve as directors or officers of any company devoted to profit-making, with the following exceptions: companies owned by an employee’s family with written consent of editor in chief or president; otherwise as approved in writing by the editor in chief or president of ProPublica.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serving in profit-making company leadership roles requires written approval to avoid conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of ProPublica affiliation externally
rubrics_metrics.description: No ProPublica employee should permit their ProPublica affiliation to be noted in any outside organization’s materials or activities without the express written approval of the editor in chief, a managing editor or the president, unless the employee serves as a representative of ProPublica or the affiliation is merely noted as part of a broader description of the employee’s identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects reputation and prevents implied endorsement; obtain approval before using affiliation publicly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political activity limits for editorial employees
rubrics_metrics.description: ProPublica does not contribute to political campaigns or parties, and editorial employees should refrain from making political contributions or participating in partisan politics — including signing petitions, attending marches or rallies, displaying lawn signs, wearing campaign paraphernalia or displaying any other form of political partisanship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial personnel may participate in issue-oriented activities (e.g., supporting human rights) but should avoid partisan activity and be mindful events can take on partisan tones; overall guidance: when in doubt, ask.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation in civic/charitable organizations with limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Participation in civic, charitable, religious, public, social or residential organizations is permitted and encouraged to the extent that they do not detract from work, are disclosed (in the case of board memberships), do not cause ProPublica to subsidize or appear to subsidize the activity, and do not otherwise violate this code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a conflict arises between an outside organization and ProPublica interests, the employee should refrain from participating in the conflicting activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of prior or current donations/time to organizations covered
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial personnel whose stories involve organizations to which they have donated money or time, either while working at ProPublica or before, should disclose that fact to their editor as soon as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If donations/time were substantial enough that a reasonable reader might question motives, discuss disclosing a note attached to the story or reassigning the employee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business-side staff conduct expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Business-side employees should be mindful that their actions may reflect on ProPublica and should not conflict with ProPublica’s core mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When in doubt, business-side employees should discuss potential concerns with a supervisor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance, training and annual attestation
rubrics_metrics.description: All employees shall be required to read this code at the outset of their employment, at the time this code is issued or updated, and once a year thereafter, and to attest in writing that they have done so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal reading and attestation create accountability and ensure awareness of the code's requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement and disciplinary consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Any lapse in judgment within the areas covered here may be considered serious enough to warrant discipline up to and including dismissal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ProPublica takes the code seriously and treats violations accordingly; supervisors must report suspected violations to the president.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting channels, confidentiality, and investigation procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: ProPublica maintains an open-door policy; employees should share questions, concerns, suggestions or complaints with someone who can address them. Supervisors and managers are required to report suspected violations of this code to the president. Violations or suspected violations may be submitted confidentially or anonymously. Reports will be promptly investigated and appropriate corrective action taken if warranted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If uncomfortable speaking with a supervisor or unsatisfied with response, employees can contact HR, the president, editor in chief or board chair. Reports will be kept confidential to the extent possible consistent with investigation needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good-faith requirement for complainants and penalties for malicious allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone filing a complaint must be acting in good faith and have reasonable grounds for believing the information indicates a violation. Allegations that prove not to be substantiated and were made maliciously or knowingly false will be viewed as a serious disciplinary offense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages responsible reporting and deters malicious false accusations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whistleblower and anti-retaliation protection
rubrics_metrics.description: No employee or director who in good faith reports a violation of this code will suffer harassment, retaliation or adverse employment consequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An employee who retaliates against someone who has reported a violation in good faith is subject to discipline up to and including dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage consultation — 'When in doubt, ask.'
rubrics_metrics.description: Everyone affiliated with ProPublica is encouraged to discuss matters within the ambit of this code and to make that discussion a continuing part of our work. When in doubt, ask.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated guidance throughout the code: employees should consult supervisors, HR, or management whenever unsure how the code applies to a situation.
